recipes.name: Pigeon Pie with Wild Game inspired by Game of Thrones
ingredients: 1 pound wild boar, cut into 2 inch pieces
1 pound rabbit, cut into 2 inch pieces
1/4 cup dried cherries, soaked in madeira wine
1/2 cup sliced mushrooms, sautéed in butter
1/4 cup apple, finely chopped, sautéed in butter
6 slices of bacon, cut in half
instructions: In a medium bowl, combine half of the squab breasts with onion, rosemary, thyme, soaked cherries, salt, and freshly ground pepper. Set aside, and repeat with wild boar: onion, garlic, rosemary, thyme, salt, and pepper. With the remaining squab breasts, combine the apple, sage, thyme, salt, and pepper. Finally, with the rabbit, combine mushrooms, thyme, and rosemary. Keep all meats separate. - 2 pounds squab breasts - 1 pound wild boar cut into 2 inch pieces - 1 tsp salt - 2 tbsp finely chopped thyme - 3 cloves garlic crushed - 2 tsp finely chopped sage - 2 tbsp finely chopped rosemary - ¼ cup apple finely chopped, sautéed in butter - ½ cup sliced mushrooms sautéed in butter - 1 pound rabbit cut into 2 inch pieces - ½ vidalia onion diced and sautéed

Preheat oven to 400°F. Whisk together flours and salt in a large bowl. Bring lard and water to a bare simmer and add to the flour, stirring with a wooden spoon until a shaggy dough forms. Once it’s cool enough to handle, knead until it forms a smooth, tacky dough. Roll out 2/3 of the dough to a 24-inch round, covering the remainder with a warm/damp towel, and drape over a liberally-greased and floured springform mold. Gently coax the dough down into the mold and press into the corners, patching as necessary to seal it. Begin filling the pastry - first with the cherry squab, a layer of bacon strips, then the wild boar, another layer of bacon, the apple squab, another layer of bacon, and the rabbit. Make sure the meat is pressed deeply into every corner, and roll out a knob of dough until it’s the size of a lid for the pastry. Cover and pinch the edges, sealing like a pie. Brush a little of the beaten egg over the top. Cut a steam hole in the center of the lid, and decorate as desired with remaining pastry. - 3 ½ ounces bread flour - 16 ounces all purpose flour - ¼ cup dried cherries soaked in madeira wine - 6 slices of bacon cut in half - ¼ cup apple finely chopped, sautéed in butter - 7 ounces water - 6 ounces lard - 1 egg beaten

Bake pie for 30 minutes at 400°F, then lower the temperature to 325°F, baking for an additional 90 minutes, or until pastry is browned and filling reaches 165°F internally. Trim the crust as necessary so the springform can eventually release - allow to cool for at least 2 hours before attempting to remove, ideally refrigerating overnight. Slice and serve with grain mustard. - Grain mustard (optional)
